name: colonies-01-hpc-readiness
title: HPC scaling readiness for the colony composite
description:
Build phase fixed daughter-process hydration so structural _add instantiates
daughter EcoliWCMs through the engine. Decide-phase N-sweep (N ∈ {1,2,4,8}) on
one machine measured per-tick wall, per-cell cost, peak RSS, and pymunk step,
extrapolated to a cells-per-HPC-node budget, and identified the GIL as the
dominant bottleneck. Output: 384 cells/node on 64-core/256GB.

visualizations.name: colony-animation
visualizations.description:
Animated GIF of a pure-WC N=2 colony, force-divided after warmup
into 4 daughters. Each capsule = one cell; colour encodes lineage
(daughters are hue-shifted variants of the mother). Regenerate via
`python studies/colonies-01-hpc-readiness/sims/make_gif.py`.

visualizations.name: perf-tick-wall-vs-n
visualizations.description:
Per-tick wall time vs N (steady-state). Linear scaling = HPC-ready;
any super-linear bend would mean GIL contention or O(N²) physics.

visualizations.name: perf-per-cell-vs-n
visualizations.description:
Per-cell wall time vs N. The per-cell-cost-within-2x-reference test
passes when this stays flat (≤ 2× the N=1 value).

visualizations.name: perf-rss-vs-n
visualizations.description: Peak RSS vs N. Slope sets the per-node cell ceiling on HPC.

visualizations.name: perf-tick-trace-largest
visualizations.description:
Per-tick wall trace for the largest-N run — exposes warmup,
division spikes, and steady-state variance.

purpose.question:
Is the pure whole-cell colony composite ready to scale on HPC? Can N
parallel EcoliWCMs grow and divide cleanly for ≥2 generations inside one
composite, and how does wall-time / RAM / per-tick cost scale with N on one
machine — well enough to project a cells-per-HPC-node budget?
purpose.mechanism:
The `colony` composite generator (v2ecoli/composites/colony.py) wires N
copies of EcoliWCM (v2ecoli/bridge.py) into a pymunk 2D physics environment.
Each EcoliWCM holds an internal Composite of the 55-process baseline. At cell
division the bridge returns a structural update (_remove mother, _add two
daughter EcoliWCMs) that the outer composite engine must hydrate. We sweep
N ∈ {1,2,4,8} and instrument per-tick costs.
purpose.expected_outcome:
After the Build fix, a pure-WC N=2 colony runs past first division to 4
ticking cells without the manual-hydration workaround in
reports/colony_report.py. In the N-sweep, per-cell wall stays within ~2× of
the N=1 cost (no super-linear blow-up from coupling/contention), peak RSS
scales close to linear, and we can name the dominant bottleneck (GIL, pymunk
serial step, or RAM-per-cell).

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
Build-phase acceptance test passes (N=2 pure-WC → 4 daughters,
no manual hydration) AND the N-sweep completes for at least
N ∈ {1,2,4}. N=8 is best-effort on a laptop and may be deferred
to the HPC follow-up.
pipeline_gate.blocks_until_resolved:
If daughter EcoliWCMs cannot be hydrated through the composite
engine's structural _add path, the colonies-02 HPC deployment
study should NOT start — there is no point sizing nodes for a
composite that loses cells at every division. Resolution choices:
(a) fix the bridge's structural-update emission so the engine
hydrates daughters natively, (b) fix the engine's _add handling
for process nodes, or (c) accept the manual-driving pattern
and re-design the HPC plan around per-cell processes outside
the composite.

simulation_set.name: bio-1cell-natural-division
simulation_set.condition: pure-WC, 1 cell, run past one natural division

modified_processes.name: EcoliWCM._handle_division
modified_processes.why:
Current emission of {agents: {_remove, _add}} does not appear to
hydrate daughter EcoliWCMs through the outer composite engine
(reports/colony_report.py works around this by manually building
standalone EcoliWCMs for daughter IDs). Fix is required for Build
acceptance.

model_change.notes:
No biological model changes. The only code work is (a) fix daughter
hydration in the colony composite, (b) build the perf harness as a
sim driver under sims/.

key_assumptions: Pure-WC colony at N=2 is feasible to run past 2 generations within ~90 min sim time on a developer laptop (40-min doubling × 2 + slack).
The dominant per-tick cost is the inner EcoliWCM update, not pymunk integration (validated by per-tick split in the harness).
Peak RSS measured with psutil after each run captures the steady-state RAM cost per cell accurately enough for HPC extrapolation (±20%).

Single-machine N-sweep extrapolates monotonically to per-node HPC sizing — i.e. no surprise breakdowns from network or filesystem at HPC scale that aren't visible here. (This is the assumption colonies-02 will test directly.)

readouts.name: colony_cell_count
readouts.description:
Number of live agents in the colony at each tick (live cell IDs in
state['cells'] or state['agents'] — depends on the composite's wiring).

readouts.name: per_cell_dry_mass
readouts.description:
Per-cell dry mass series, from each cell's `mass` store driven by
EcoliWCM._read_outputs.

readouts.name: division_events
readouts.description:
Per-cell wall-clock + sim-time stamps of division events, recorded
by the perf harness when it observes the {_remove, _add} structural
update on the cells map.

readouts.name: wall_seconds
readouts.description: End-to-end wall time of the run.

readouts.name: peak_rss_mb
readouts.description: Peak resident set size of the run process, via psutil.

readouts.name: per_tick_latency_ms
readouts.description:
Distribution of wall-time per composite tick (one row per tick in
runs.db). Reduced to {p50, p95, p99, max} in the Decide report.

readouts.name: per_cell_update_ms
readouts.description:
Time spent inside each EcoliWCM.update() per tick, summed over cells.
Captured by monkey-patching EcoliWCM.update in the harness, or by a
lightweight timing decorator.

readouts.name: pymunk_step_ms
readouts.description:
Time spent inside the pymunk physics step per tick. Same instrumentation
pattern as per_cell_update_ms but on the multibody process.

behavior_tests.name: daughters-hydrated
behavior_tests.description:
After the first division event in the build-smoke-n2 run, both
daughter agent IDs appear in the cells map AND both continue to
advance (mass changes, EcoliWCM.update called) on subsequent ticks
without the manual standalone-WCM workaround that exists in
reports/colony_report.py.

behavior_tests.name: two-generations-complete
behavior_tests.description:
Pure-WC N=2 colony reaches ≥4 live cells by end of run (both
mothers divided), with all four cells advancing on the final tick.

behavior_tests.name: reference-perf-recorded
behavior_tests.description:
The N=1 reference run completed and recorded wall_seconds + peak_rss_mb
+ per_tick_latency series — i.e. the perf harness is wired and writing
rows into runs.db.

behavior_tests.name: per-cell-cost-within-2x-reference
behavior_tests.description:
For each N>1 sweep run, the per-cell wall-time (wall_seconds / N_cells_at_end)
is at most 2× the N=1 reference per-cell wall-time. Catches super-linear
blow-up that would block HPC scaling.

if_primary_tests_pass.implementation_status:
colony composite is HPC-ready: daughter hydration works through
the engine, per-cell cost stays bounded as N grows on one machine.
pipeline_unblocks: colonies-02-hpc-deployment can size HPC nodes from the recorded peak_rss_mb and per_cell_update_ms numbers.

diagnose: If daughters-hydrated FAILS, the engine's structural-update path for nested processes is the root issue. Look at how `_add` is consumed and whether the daughter's `address: local:EcoliWCM` gets instantiated.

If per-cell-cost-within-2x-reference FAILS, profile which timer grew super-linearly (per_cell_update_ms — GIL contention; pymunk_step_ms — O(N²) physics broadphase; total wall but not per-cell — scheduler overhead).

limitations: Single-machine only; cross-node HPC scaling is colonies-02's job.
90 min sim window is one full doubling plus a buffer for the second division, not an N-generation run.
Per-cell EcoliWCM internal cache is shared (same cache_dir path); RAM extrapolation may underestimate HPC RAM if HPC runs use per-cell caches.
pymunk is single-threaded; GIL contention may dominate before any HPC-relevant bottleneck shows up.

implementation_requirements.title: studies/colonies-01-hpc-readiness/sims/run.py perf harness
implementation_requirements.description:
A driver that takes (sim_name, n_cells, duration_min, seed), builds
the colony composite, runs it tick-by-tick, and writes per-tick rows
to studies/colonies-01-hpc-readiness/runs.db with these columns:
tick, sim_time, wall_ms, per_cell_update_ms_sum, pymunk_step_ms,
live_cell_count, rss_mb. Also writes one row to a `runs` table per
completed run with totals.
steps: Decide DB schema (one ticks table, one runs table).
Wrap EcoliWCM.update + pymunk step with timing.
Add a --sim-name flag matching simulation_set entries.

implementation_requirements.title: Hydrate daughter EcoliWCMs through the composite engine on structural _add
implementation_requirements.description:
Today reports/colony_report.py manually instantiates standalone EcoliWCMs
for daughter cell IDs (~lines 520-540) because the structural _add
inside EcoliWCM._handle_division doesn't appear to make the engine run
daughters as embedded processes. Fix the bridge OR the engine wiring
so daughters tick normally after division.
steps: Reproduce the issue with a minimal pure-WC N=2 run and capture exactly what the engine does (or doesn't do) at the division tick.
Decide whether the fix is in EcoliWCM._handle_division (different update shape) or in how the colony document declares `cells` (must accept process nodes via _add).

conclusion:
Phase = Decide. Pipeline-open to colonies-02-hpc-deployment with the caveats
below.

Build-phase fixes required to get here:

1. viva-munk apply_updates_with_realize unpacked 2 values from
   bigraph_schema.core.realize, which now returns 3 (escape_merges), so every
   structural `_add` crashed. Patched (viva-munk branch
   rename-multi-cell-to-viva-munk, commit "fix: handle 3-tuple return from
   bigraph_schema core.realize").
2. v2ecoli/colony.py wired only `mass`/`volume`/`exchange` outputs on initial
   cells. `_handle_division` writes to `agents`, but with no `agents` wire the
   update had nowhere to land, so mothers stayed put. Fixed by mirroring the
   full daughter wiring (`agent_id`/`location`/`angle` inputs, `length`/`agents`
   outputs).
3. v2ecoli/bridge.py `_handle_division` hard-coded
   `interval=self.config.get('interval', 60.0)` for daughters; `interval` is
   not in `config_schema`, so the fallback always won and daughters ticked once
   per 60s instead of inheriting the mother's 1s cadence. Fixed by passing
   `interval` through.

After all three fixes, a pure-WC N=2 colony with both initial cells
force-divided produces 4 hydrated daughters that all advance.

Perf findings (steady-state, N ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8}, 60-tick window):

- Per-cell wall is flat at 70-74 ms across N=1..8 (slight decrease with N as
  Python/import overhead amortizes); per-cell-cost-within-2x-reference passes
  at all N.
- pymunk is essentially free (<0.2 ms/tick even at N=8). All cost is the inner
  EcoliWCM composite (55 biological steps × N cells, walked sequentially in one
  Python thread).
- RSS grows ~450 MB per added cell, atop a ~1 GB Python baseline.

Bottleneck at scale is the GIL: process-bigraph composites are single-threaded,
so one process uses ~1 CPU core regardless of cell count. Scaling to many cells
means scaling processes, not cells-per-process.

HPC node sizing (64-core / 256 GB target):

- RAM-limited ceiling per node: 256 GB / 0.45 GB ≈ 570 cells (RAM-bound, single
  process — not practical at speed).
- CPU-limited realtime ceiling per process: ~13 cells (13 × 73 ms ≈ 950 ms,
  ~realtime).
- Recommendation: 8 cells/process × 64 processes = 512 cells/node uses
  64 × (1 GB + 8 × 0.45 GB) = ~290 GB, just over budget. Drop to
  6 cells/process × 64 = 384 cells/node, fits 256 GB with ~10% headroom;
  per-process tick wall ~440 ms (~2× realtime).

Not validated here (handed to colonies-02):

- Cross-node scaling, distributed environment field.
- Process-bigraph composite parallelism within a single process (unsupported;
  needs engine work).
- Multi-generation drift in per-tick cost (daughters' internal composites may
  bloat over many divisions).
- Per-cell ParCa cache contention if processes share cache_dir.

Memory (2026-07-26 leak hunt): the per-tick RSS growth in the long N=1 run
(finding F-06) is now characterised, not an unbounded native leak. It is
localized to the inner WCM's elongation step (~82%) + mass-listener (~17%),
with only ~0.2 MB/tick truly retained (scipy LSODA work arrays) and the rest
macOS allocator arena churn. On Linux (glibc) the growth is 0.017 MB/tick
unfixed and 0.000 with periodic malloc_trim(0), versus ~1.6 MB/tick on the
macOS mini, so memory on the HPC target is bounded and the cells-per-node
budget stands. The "unbounded native leak" framing was substantially a macOS
measurement artifact.

Role: this study is Part A - enabling compute infrastructure (correct
division, flat per-cell cost, Linux-bounded memory) for the phenotype-first
colonies investigation. The memory behaviour is a characterised, Linux-bounded,
mitigated footnote, not the result and not an HPC blocker.

followup_proposals.title: Cross-node HPC deployment of the colony composite
followup_proposals.motivation:
Build acceptance and N-sweep both PASS on one machine. Per-cell cost
is flat, pymunk is free, RAM grows linearly. Single-process is the
right starting shape on HPC; orchestration is the remaining design.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
colonies-01-hpc-readiness.gate_status == passed AND
per_cell_ms and per_cell_rss recorded.

followup_proposals.title: Multi-generation perf drift study
followup_proposals.motivation:
The N-sweep here uses N initial cells held static. Real HPC workloads
will have growing colonies (each division doubles N). We need to know
whether per-cell wall stays at 73 ms or drifts as daughter EcoliWCM
internal composites accumulate history / fragment caches / etc.
The 2026-07-26 leak hunt has since characterised the F-06 RSS growth as
localized (elongation + mass-listener) and Linux-bounded, so this is no
longer a "fix the native leak before HPC" blocker; the residual
~0.2 MB/tick scipy LSODA retention is the remaining small optimization
target this follow-up can quantify over natural divisions.
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism:
Per-cell wall drifts ≤ 20% across gens 0-4 of a natural-division
colony (~10000s sim). If drift > 20%, the inner composite is
accumulating dead nodes or growing per-tick allocations.

followup_proposals.title: Per-cell ParCa cache contention
followup_proposals.motivation:
All cells in this study share `out/cache`. If HPC processes also share
cache, file-system contention may show up at scale and silently
degrade per-cell perf. If per-process caches are needed, each cell
adds ~the full ParCa cache footprint to RAM/disk.

followup_proposals.title: Make process-bigraph composite engine GIL-aware (research)
followup_proposals.motivation:
Every process in a composite ticks on one thread. For embarrassingly-
parallel composites (independent cells), free parallelism is on the
table if the engine supports concurrent process invocations
(multiprocessing or thread-per-process with GIL-friendly bodies).
Engine-level question that won't unblock colonies-02 but is worth
scoping.

findings.statement:
Per-cell wall time is flat at 70–74 ms across N ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8} (slight
decrease with N as Python/import overhead amortizes). Composite scales
linearly on one machine.

expected.summary: per-cell wall stays within 2× of the N=1 reference; flat is the strongest pass condition.

findings.next_action: Use 73 ms/tick/cell as the projection input for colonies-02-hpc-deployment.

findings.statement:
The GIL is the dominant bottleneck at colony scale. Process-bigraph
composites are single-threaded by design — one process uses ~1 CPU core
regardless of how many cells it holds. Scaling means more processes, not
more cells/process.

evidence.observed: pymunk_step_ms ≈ 0.1 ms/tick (free); ecoli_ms grows linearly with N

findings.explanation:
All 55 inner WCM steps are walked sequentially in one Python thread.
pymunk is free even at N=8, so any super-linear cost would have to be in
the EcoliWCM update — but per-cell stays flat. The only ceiling visible
is total wall vs realtime per process, which crosses ~1.0 around N≈13.

findings.statement:
Steady-state per-cell RSS is ~450 MB, atop a ~1 GB Python baseline
(ParCa + WCM imports + cached numpy arrays).

expected.summary:
Linear in N up to N=8 within one process. Sets the per-node cell
ceiling on HPC: 6 cells/process × 64 processes = ~290 GB on a 256 GB
node; drop to 5-6 cells/process for headroom → ~384 cells/node.

findings.statement:
pymunk 2D physics is essentially free at the N values we tested
(≤ 0.2 ms/tick at N=8). All wall-time cost is the inner EcoliWCM.

Three independent bugs blocked daughter hydration through the engine
and had to be fixed before the Decide phase could run.
findings.explanation:
(1) viva-munk apply_updates_with_realize unpacked 2 values from
bigraph_schema.core.realize, which now returns 3 (escape_merges) —
every structural _add crashed.
(2) v2ecoli/colony.py wired only mass/volume/exchange outputs on
initial cells; _handle_division writes to `agents` with no wire,
so mother updates had nowhere to land.
(3) v2ecoli/bridge.py _handle_division hard-coded `interval=60.0` for

evidence.observed: After all three fixes, pure-WC N=2 force-divided to 4 hydrated daughters that all advance on the next tick.

findings.statement:
RSS grows continuously during a single long N=1 run at ~5 MB/sim-second
(1126 MB at tick 0 → 7016 MB by tick 1050, before division). Originally read as
either accumulating state in the EcoliWCM internal composite or a leak;
visible only in long runs, not in the 60s N-sweep windows.

Characterised by the 2026-07-26 leak hunt (supersedes the leak framing): the
growth is localized to the inner WCM's polypeptide-elongation step (~82%) +
mass-listener (~17%), and is NOT an unbounded native leak. Only ~0.2 MB/tick is
truly retained (tracemalloc-visible: scipy LSODA integrator work arrays held
per solve); the remainder is macOS allocator arena churn — large per-tick numpy
working arrays that are freed but not returned to the OS. Linux validation (glibc
container) showed RSS growth of only 0.017 MB/tick with no fix and 0.000 with
periodic malloc_trim(0), versus ~1.6 MB/tick on the macOS mini. On the Linux HPC
target the colony's memory is bounded, so the cells-per-node budget stands; the
~5 MB/s reading here was substantially a macOS measurement artifact.

evidence.observed: rss_mb climbs monotonically across the pre-division window

findings.next_action:
Source identified (elongation + mass-listener; scipy LSODA retention);
growth is Linux-bounded. Residual ~0.2 MB/tick scipy retention is a small
optimization target (solver reuse / method change / periodic malloc_trim),
tracked in the multi-gen-perf-drift follow-up.
